# Chapter 3 — sketch answers {.unnumbered}

\(1\) Tools without a system leave gaps nobody owns --- nobody owns patching;
security depends on a few people remembering things --- the admin account
without MFA that nobody checked; nothing connects risk, controls and improvement
--- no record of what was decided or why. (2) Plan: Assess R3 and decide the
customer database must be encrypted with strictly limited access. Do: Implement
encryption (A.8.24) and tighten access rights. Check: The internal audit finds a
database export routine writing unencrypted copies to a shared folder. Act:
Encrypt or remove the export, restrict the folder, and add the routine to the
next audit's checklist. (3) Clause 6 is Plan --- the risk assessment and
treatment decisions for R1--R3; Clause 8 is Do --- running the planned processes
and implementing treatment; Clause 9 is Check --- internal audit and management
review; Clause 10 is Act --- corrective action such as automating
de-provisioning. (4) Not defensible as stated: The checkout is where FastGoods'
revenue and payment risk live (R2), and using a provider transfers work, not
accountability. The auditor would call it scope gaming --- the boundary drawn to
dodge the real risk --- and require the payment flow, including the provider
relationship, inside the scope. (5) Applies: A.8.5 Secure authentication ---
logins need MFA --- linked to R1. Excluded: A.7.4 Physical security monitoring
--- FastGoods runs no data centre of its own; the cloud provider's physical
controls are covered through the supplier relationship (Lecture 19).
